A1.justification: Despite the changed title and format, both PDFs present the same AGRPO research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original AGRPO training results on GSM8K, MATH, and Countdown, an inference-step experiment, and sample responses.

after.justification: V2 reports original results on four reasoning tasks, additional ablations, training-time measurements, and sample responses.

M1.justification: The core AGRPO objective and intermediate-state likelihood computation remain. V2 Section 4.2.2 adds entropy-weighted timestep sampling with an importance-weight correction, extending the existing Monte Carlo variance-reduction scheme without replacing the algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds training and evaluation on 4x4 Sudoku, extending coverage to grid-based constraint planning. Its MATH results also include GSM8K-to-MATH transfer and a MATH-trained comparison, replacing v1's reported OpenMathInstruct-2-trained model.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LLaDA 1.5, wd1, and SPG, while removing the diffusion CoT SFT and UniGRPO comparisons. Diffu-GRPO and the autoregressive comparisons remain. The inference-frontier comparison also adds LLaDA 1.5 and drops diffu-GRPO.

E3.justification: V2 standardizes training at response length 384 and 128 sampling steps, changing v1's GSM8K and Countdown configurations. Training temperature changes to 0.6 and semi-autoregressive block length to 12, from 0.5/0.9 and 24/32 respectively. Table 1 now evaluates both 256- and 512-token outputs for every task; new ablation and timing experiments introduce additional controlled settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds measured ablations on Monte Carlo sample count, a joint ablation of low-discrepancy and entropy-based sampling, and computational-cost comparisons (Figures 3–4 and Table 2). These substantially extend v1's qualitative discussion of stability and compute tradeoffs. The appendix sample-response case is also replaced and analyzed.

E5.justification: V2 introduces shaded training-reward variability in Figures 3–4, described as within-run variance or standard deviation over 15-step rolling windows. V1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. Neither version reports independent-seed confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially replaces and expands the results: v1 reports AGRPO accuracies of 87.3/40.8/40.0 on GSM8K/MATH/Countdown; v2 reports 88.1/42.0/82.4/95.2 at length 512 on GSM8K/MATH-500/Countdown/Sudoku. Changed training and evaluation conditions prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. V2 also adds ablation and timing results; its claimed 1.4-point GSM8K margin does not match the listed 88.1 versus 84.5.

T1.justification: V1 derives AGRPO by rewriting the GRPO sum as a timestep expectation. V2 substantially revises this reasoning through formal MDP and policy-gradient definitions and an explicit denoising-trajectory derivation. Appendix A adds the entropy-weighted estimator and Theorem A.1 proving its unbiasedness for the unclipped objective.

C1.justification: The central claims of tractable, unbiased AGRPO and improved inference tradeoffs remain. V2 recasts the contribution around multi-step denoising policy gradients rather than a faithful GRPO adaptation, and extends its headline efficacy claim to Sudoku with revised performance margins. Fourfold sampling acceleration was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for GSM8K training outperforming MATH training, attributes baseline discrepancies to prompting and parsing, and argues that denser learning signals offset additional computation. Appendix G adds interpretations of robustness to generation artifacts and expands the retained entropy-collapse limitation with possible mitigations.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents hardware, training duration, reward construction, global batch size, clipping and KL settings, checkpoint selection, TRL usage, and inference/training sampling-mask consistency. Code release is planned, not established. Conversely, v1's learning rate, AdamW coefficients, and LoRA scaling/dropout details are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the focused diffu-GRPO/UniGRPO critique with substantially broader positioning in Section 6 and Appendix C. It adds substantive discussions of wd1, VRPO, DCoLT, SPG, and related policy-gradient research, distinguishing AGRPO through its multi-step formulation and timestep sampling.

P1.justification: The title changes to Simple Policy Gradients for Reasoning with Diffusion Language Models. Extensive rewriting reorganizes the argument around MDPs and policy gradients, introduces a dedicated related-work section, and redistributes practical considerations and limitations across Appendices A–G.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text and bibliography, redraws Figure 1, removes v1's pretraining schematic, and redesigns the inference plot and benchmark table. It adds ablation plots and timing/comparison tables, while substantially reformatting the appendix sample responses.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for AGRPO's stability and computational tradeoffs: Figures 3–4 and Appendix B test claims that v1 mostly discussed qualitatively. The explicit MDP derivation, estimator proof, and broader benchmark comparisons also improve the paper's foundation. These gains outweigh the loss of some optimizer details and the inconsistent GSM8K margin claim, although heterogeneous imported baseline results still limit comparative conclusions.
